deviation: `java.util.Date` reading and `@JsonFormat` pattern and time-zone writes are in `JavaUtilDateModule` (`flint.jackson.databind.module_`). Plain Date writes are built in. Two places register the module: Flint AOT's generated `JsonMapperBuilderCustomizer`, whenever the application's described types hold a `Date`, and the templated `ObjectMapper` methods (`readValue!T`, `treeToValue!T`, `convertValue!T`, `writeValueAsString!T`, `writeValueAsBytes!T`, `writeValue!T`, `ObjectWriter.writeValueAsString!T`) when `T` holds one at any depth. One path remains: Flint's erased methods (`readValue(content, typeName)`, `convertValue(Any, typeName)`) on a mapper built by hand over descriptors the user added, for a type holding a `Date`, without `addModule`. Spring code cannot reach it, since it names types by `Class<T>` (`readValue!T`) or uses Boot's mapper. That path throws `InvalidDefinitionException`: "`java.util.Date` is read, and formatted with a @JsonFormat pattern or time zone, by JavaUtilDateModule, which this mapper does not have: register it with JsonMapper.builder().addModule(new JavaUtilDateModule()) (deviation D-JACKSON-10)". The test "java.util.Date: plain writes need no module; erased reads without one name JavaUtilDateModule (D-JACKSON-10)" in framework/jackson-databind/tests/java_util_date_test.d pins it. When `readerFor` or `TypeReference` are ported, they must register the module the same way the templated methods do, with tests.
reason: Jackson builds Date support into every mapper; linking it everywhere costs every web app about 70 KB of calendar and parsing code, when the error body only writes a Date. A build-time check on the erased path would have to make `JsonMapper.Builder.descriptors()` reference the module, which links it into every application and defeats pay-for-use.
